name: Badge
title: Badge
summary: Small pill labels: the React `Badge` section tag in an outlined pill, `.badge` status badges, removable `.cr-tag` filters and the `.count` number dot.
whenToUse: React `Badge`: tag a section or promo in the app ("YOU'RE ALMOST DONE!", "GET A SNEAK PEEK", "Trending").
`.badge`: show a status beside data (Draft, New, Live, Pending, Failed, Partner).
`.cr-tag`: show an applied filter the user can remove.
`.count`: unread or pending numbers on a tab, nav item or icon.
On website sections, use Eyebrow (`.eyebrow`) to label a section, not a badge.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a badge as a button; badges are labels. Use Chip for toggles.

props.name: tone
props.description: `outlineDark` on dark, `outlineLight` on light, `solidBlue` filled, `accentText` blue text with no border.

react.notes: `import { Badge, StatusBadge, Tag, Count } from '@ism/ui'` (source: `packages/react/src/components/Badge.tsx`). `Badge`: small uppercase, wide-tracked eyebrow label inside a thin outlined pill, ISM's signature way to tag a section ("YOU'RE ALMOST DONE!", "GET A SNEAK PEEK"). Styled inline; extra `span` attributes and `style` are passed through. The other three render the HTML classes below:

props.name: tone
props.description: `outlineDark` on dark, `outlineLight` on light, `solidBlue` filled, `accentText` blue text with no border.

props.name: children
props.description: The label; rendered uppercase for Latin script. Short and warm: "Trending", "You're almost done!".

variantNotes: Sizes: 24px (`.cr-badge-sm` for 12px text as on data tables), `.cr-badge-md` 28px. Add `.cr-badge-dot` for a leading dot.
Tags: 32px; the 24px × has a 44px invisible hit area. States: hover ×, focus ×, disabled (`.cr-tag-off` + `disabled`), applied (`.cr-tag-active`, info tint).
Live: `.live-dot` (`--live`) inside a badge for on-air.

states.universal: See rules/states.md for the seven required states and their hooks.

rules: Always pair colour with a word. Never colour alone.
Use status colours only for status: `--success`, `--error`, `--warning`, `--info` with their `-bg`.
Counts and notification dots are Horizon Blue (`.count`), never red.
`solidBlue` / `.cr-solid-info` are rare; do not place them next to a blue primary button.
Live / on-air is the only use of `--live`.
Keep badges to one line, no wrapping (`white-space:nowrap`).
do: React `Badge`: tag a section or promo in the app ("YOU'RE ALMOST DONE!", "GET A SNEAK PEEK", "Trending").

Use status colours only for status: `--success`, `--error`, `--warning`, `--info` with their `-bg`.
Counts and notification dots are Horizon Blue (`.count`), never red.
`solidBlue` / `.cr-solid-info` are rare; do not place them next to a blue primary button.

dont: Do not use a badge as a button; badges are labels. Use Chip for toggles.
accessibility: A status badge is text; screen readers read it as-is. Do not add `role="status"` unless it updates live.
`.count` needs context: put it inside the labelled link, or add visually hidden text ("3 unread").
Every tag remove button has `aria-label="Remove <name>"`; after removing, move focus to the next tag or the field.
content: One word for status: Draft, New, Live, Pending, Failed, Partner.
React Badge copy is short and warm: "Trending", "You're almost done!", "Get a sneak peek", "500+ languages".
Tags show the item name as the user chose it: "Amharic", "dot.Bible app".
